belief: One more sin and God will give up on me.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that one more sin will make God give up on you, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: A parent or authority who gave “last chances” and then gave up. Threats that you would lose God’s love if you kept failing. Long struggles with a habit that make you feel God must be running out of patience. Fear-based teaching about falling away. Relationships where one mistake ended everything.
teaches: God’s faithfulness does not depend on yours. Even when we are faithless, He remains faithful. He has promised never to leave or forsake His children. When a believer falls, the LORD holds his hand. Nothing in all creation can separate you from God’s love in Christ, and the God who began a good work in you will finish it. Sin is serious, and God may discipline you, but He does not give up on His children.
self_statements: If I mess up again, God is done with me.
God’s patience must be almost gone.
I have to be perfect from now on, or I’m lost.
God gives up on people like me.
One more failure and it’s over.
errors: Picturing God like people who gave up on you.
Treating the next mistake as the end of everything.
Believing you are either perfect or rejected.
Predicting that God will abandon you.
questions: What does Romans 8:38–39 say can separate me from God’s love?
If I am faithless, what does God remain?
Who in my life gave up on me, and am I picturing God like them?
What does God promise in Hebrews 13:5?
When a believer falls, who holds his hand?
Does fear of God giving up make me stronger or more anxious?
Who promised to finish the work in me?
truth: God will not give up on me. Nothing in all creation can separate me from His love in Christ. Even when I am faithless, He remains faithful. When I fall, He holds my hand. My sin is serious, and He may correct me, but He will never leave me or forsake me.
hw_questions: What can separate me from God’s love?
If I am faithless, what does God remain?
Am I picturing God like someone who gave up on me?
What does God promise in Hebrews 13:5?
When I fall, who holds my hand?

hw_truths: Nothing can separate me from God’s love in Christ.
Even when I am faithless, He remains faithful.
God will never leave me or forsake me.
When I fall, the LORD holds my hand.
God does not give up on His children.
God will finish the work He began in me.
log: Each day, write one way God has been faithful to me, even when I was not.
name_example: Sarah’s steps are ordered by the LORD who takes delight in her journey. Though she falls, she will not be overwhelmed, for the LORD is holding her hand.
actions: After a failure, confess it, then write:
“God has not given up on me,” and take one good next step.
Write a list of times you fell and God restored you,
and keep it where you can see it.
about a time they failed and God did not give up on them.
prayer: Father, thank You that nothing can separate me from Your love in Christ. Help me reject the lie that one more sin will make You give up on me. When I fall, hold my hand and lift me up. Thank You for remaining faithful even when I am faithless. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
songs: God’s forgiveness addresses lingering guilt and fear of condemnation.
Grace offers a new beginning rather than defining a person by failure.
God’s faithful presence challenges the expectation of rejection and abandonment.
This familiar hymn places confidence in Jesus’ love rather than personal strength.
